engine reproduces the observed behavior, not the intent.

The language picker's markup. English always leads the list and carries the
empty value, because "no locale" and "American English" are the same choice.
When the picker also offers what could be downloaded, the two halves split
into named groups; otherwise every option sits in one flat list.

The attribute order is not tidy and is not ours to tidy: the English option
carries `data-installed` before `selected`, an installed translation carries
it after, and themes and plugins have been matching on that markup for
years.

Putting themes and extensions on disk. Themes come from wordpress.org
(block themes render on the engine) or an uploaded zip; extensions come
from an uploaded zip or a URL, and must carry a minn.json: a WordPress
plugin would install but never run, so it is refused with the reason.
Every archive is unpacked through one guarded routine: exactly one
top-level folder, no absolute or dotted paths, the folder's identity
checked before it is moved into place.

else the site's WPLANG, else en_US, exactly as the reference resolves it.

JED catalogs Minn Admin's language packs install under
wp-content/languages/plugins (the bundle's own languages folder is the
fallback). Installing a pack fetches the release asset the bundle's
manifest names for that locale, checks its hash, and unpacks only that
locale's files, so an eject leaves the files WordPress would have written.

classes.doc:
Update offers from wordpress.org for the site's plugins and themes: the
directory's update-check endpoints asked with the installed headers, the
answer kept in the minn_updates option (JSON) for twelve hours, and the
offers applied by downloading the release archive through the one
package unpacker. A plugin or theme the directory does not know keeps
its folder untouched and is never offered anything. The per-item
auto-update lists are the site's own auto_update_plugins and
auto_update_themes options, in the shape the app already reads.

Application passwords as the reference stores them: a serialized list in
the user's _application_passwords meta, each entry uuid, app_id, name,
password (a hash), created, last_used, last_ip. New passwords are 24
characters shown in groups of four; the stored hash is phpass, which the
reference verifies too, so a password made here survives a switch back.
A hash the reference made with its own fast scheme cannot be verified here.

classes.doc:
The three cookies a sign-in sets: the auth cookie on the admin and
plugins paths (the secure variant over HTTPS, keyed off that scheme's
salt) and the logged_in cookie on the site root, which is the one REST
reads. Every value shares the username|expiration|token|hmac shape.

methods.doc: The hash suffixed onto every cookie name: md5 of the siteurl option.

methods.doc: A non-persistent sign-in keeps the server expiry but sends session cookies the browser drops on close.

methods.doc: A cookie value under any scheme's salt (auth, secure_auth, logged_in).

classes.doc:
Why a request is not authenticated, as the reference's error code: a
missing or invalid cookie is rest_not_logged_in (the request is simply
anonymous); a good cookie with a bad nonce is rest_cookie_invalid_nonce.

classes.doc: A validated session: the user row and the raw session token behind it.

classes.doc:
Resolves the current user two ways. A page load carries the cookie alone;
a REST call must also carry a nonce bound to the same session.

methods.doc:
A REST caller: the cookie session with its nonce first; failing that,
HTTP Basic credentials carrying an application password, which need no
nonce. A wrong Basic pair is reported as not logged in.

methods.doc: The user an Authorization: Basic header's application password unlocks, with the use recorded.

methods.doc: Username and password to a user row; no session is created here.

classes.doc:
The capability engine: a user's roles from {prefix}capabilities usermeta,
the primitives those roles grant, and the meta-capability mapping for
edit_post, delete_post, and read_post.

methods.name: primitivesOf
shapes: @return array<string, true> the union of primitives the user's roles grant

methods.name: can
methods.doc: Does the user hold every primitive the (possibly meta) capability maps to?

methods.doc: The primitives a capability requires, all of which must be held.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Cookie
classes.doc:
The logged_in auth cookie: username|expiration|token|hmac, with
key  = HMAC-md5(username|fragment|expiration|token, logged_in salt)
hmac = HMAC-sha256(username|expiration|token, key)
and the session live in the user's session_tokens store.

methods.name: name
methods.doc: The cookie name this site uses: a hash of the siteurl option.

methods.name: fromJar
methods.doc:
The logged_in cookie from a request's cookie jar: the canonical name
first, then any logged_in cookie, since tooling may send a name
derived from a different host.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\LoginThrottle
classes.doc:
Failed sign-ins per address, so a password guesser meets a wall: twenty
failures in fifteen minutes and the address waits out the window. The
counters live in the options table (autoload off), one row per address,
as "window start:count"; a successful sign-in clears the row.

methods.name: retryAfter
methods.doc: Seconds the address must wait, or null when it may try.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Nonce
classes.doc:
The wp_rest nonce: ten characters of HMAC-md5(tick|wp_rest|uid|token)
under the nonce salt, accepted for the current tick and the one before.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Password
classes.doc:
The stored password scheme. A modern "$wp$2y$..." value is bcrypt over
base64(HMAC-sha384(password, "wp-sha384")); a bare "$2y$" value is plain
bcrypt. Legacy phpass "$P$" hashes are not verified.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: A stored hash in the modern scheme: "$wp" plus bcrypt over the pre-hash.

methods.name: fragment
methods.doc:
The four characters of the hash the cookie key is derived from: the
LAST four for a "$wp$" hash, offset 8 for legacy phpass. Getting this
wrong yields a cookie that verifies nowhere while every other check
passes, so both branches are pinned by the auth suite.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\PasswordReset
classes.doc:
Password reset keys in the reference's storage shape: user_activation_key
holds "time:hash", the key itself travels in the email link and is good
for a day. The hash is the engine's own ($minn$ over the nonce salt); a
key the reference issued ($generic$) is not readable here, so it is
refused and the reader asks for a fresh link.

methods.name: issue
methods.doc: Mints a key, stores its hash, returns the key for the link.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc: True when the key matches the stored hash and has not expired.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: "valid", "expired" (a matching key past its day), or "invalid".

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Phpass
classes.doc:
The portable phpass hash ($P$), from Openwall's public description of the
scheme: a log2 iteration count, an eight-character salt, and an iterated
MD5 in phpass's own base-64 alphabet. The reference still verifies these
for application passwords, which makes them the portable choice.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\PortableHash
classes.doc:
The portable phpass hash ("$P$"), the shape the reference stores in
the post-password cookie: an iteration count character, an eight
character salt, and MD5 iterated over salt and password, encoded in
phpass's own base64 alphabet. Implemented from the published algorithm
so cookies are accepted in both directions.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The reference's cookies carry 2^13 iterations; it accepts nothing weaker.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Roles
classes.doc:
Role definitions from the site's {prefix}user_roles option, parsed by a
bounded scan of the serialized blob, with the seeded contract copy as the
fallback for a fresh install.

methods.name: level
methods.doc: The wp_user_level stored beside the capabilities meta.

methods.name: serializeSingle
methods.doc: The {role: true} capabilities meta in its serialized form.

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: Drops the parsed map so the next read sees a rewritten option.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
Each role is a string key over a two-entry array of "name" and
"capabilities"; the capabilities map is {cap: bool}. Null when the
blob has another shape, so the caller can fall back.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Salts
classes.doc:
The site's own secret material, read from the constants wp-config.php
defines, so the engine keys off exactly what the install used.

methods.name: configured
methods.doc: True when every key and salt is defined and none is the installer's placeholder.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: HMAC-md5 under the scheme's salt: the primitive every cookie and nonce is built from.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\Sessions
classes.doc:
The session_tokens usermeta store: {sha256(token): {expiration, ip, ua,
login}}. Read by a bounded scan of the serialized blob and written by
serializing it ourselves, so stored data is never executed.

methods.name: generateToken
methods.doc: A 43-character token; only sha256(token) is ever stored or compared.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a session, pruning expired ones, and returns the raw token.

methods.name: destroyAll
methods.doc: Ends every session of the user (a password change).

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Removes one session; true when it existed.

methods.name: destroyKey
methods.doc: Removes the session stored under a key (the sha256 of its token); true when it existed.

methods.name: destroyOthers
methods.doc: Ends every session of the user except the one stored under the given key.

methods.name: read
shapes: @return array<string, array{expiration: int, ip: string, ua: string, login: int}>

methods.name: serialize
methods.doc: The map in PHP's serialized form, entry keys in the order given.

classes.name: Minn\Auth\TypeCapabilities
classes.doc:
The capability names a post type's permissions are built from. Posts and
pages own their families (edit_posts, edit_others_pages, ...). Navigation
menus fold every one of them onto edit_theme_options, which is why an
editor may read a menu and only an administrator may change one; the
reference's own registration says the same thing.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: A cap name built from the post/page family, folded when the type folds.

classes.name: Minn\Autoloader
classes.doc: PSR-4 for the Minn namespace: Minn\Http\Request lives at src/Minn/Http/Request.php.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Attributes
classes.doc:
The JSON object a block delimiter carries, read in place. Rewriting one
block's attributes must not disturb the rest of the markup, so callers
take the object's exact substring rather than reserializing the document.

methods.name: objectAt
methods.doc: The JSON object starting at $at, brace-matched through any strings; null when there is none.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Block
classes.doc:
One parsed block. A null name is freeform HTML between blocks. The
innerContent list holds the block's own HTML chunks in order, with a
null placeholder wherever an inner block sits.

methods.name: className
methods.doc: The class names declared on the block's own attributes (className).

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\BlockName
classes.doc: The block name rules: a string, lower-case, `namespace/name`.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Context
classes.doc:
What the template blocks render against: the resolution, the main
query's posts, and a stack of "current post" frames pushed by post
templates and comment templates as they loop.

shapes: @param list<PostRecord> $posts the main query's page of posts

methods.name: inLoop
methods.doc: Inside a post template loop (as opposed to the singular view).

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Archives
classes.doc: core/archives: the months that have published posts, newest first.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Categories
classes.doc: core/categories: the non-empty categories as a list, by name.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Dates
classes.doc: Site-local dates the way the dynamic blocks print them.

methods.name: iso
methods.doc: ISO 8601 with the site's offset, from a site-local MySQL datetime.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: The date_format option applied to a site-local MySQL datetime.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\LatestComments
classes.doc: core/latest-comments: the newest approved comments with avatar, meta, and a 20-word excerpt.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\LatestPosts
classes.doc: core/latest-posts: the newest published posts as a list, optionally dated.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Search
classes.doc:
core/search: the site search form. The button sits outside or inside
the field and shows text or the search icon; the block's colour and
font presets land on the button (font family on the input too). The
input id comes from the shared request counter.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\SocialLinks
classes.doc:
core/social-links and core/social-link. The list keeps its stored
wrapper and gains the flex layout classes; each link renders from its
parent's icon colours and the service's icon. The icons are the
reference's rendered output captured as data (src/data/social-icons.json,
the upstream set is CC0); an unknown service gets the share icon.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\SyncedPattern
classes.doc: core/block: a synced pattern, rendered from the wp_block post it references.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\TagCloud
classes.doc:
core/tag-cloud: non-empty tags by name, sized from 8pt to 22pt in
proportion to their counts (every tag at 8pt when the counts are equal).

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\Comments
classes.doc: comments, comments-title, comment-template, the comment-* blocks, and the comment form.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\Navigation
classes.doc:
navigation, navigation-link, page-list. A navigation block's items come
from its inner blocks, the wp_navigation post it references, the newest
published wp_navigation post, or (when none of those exist) the first
classic nav_menu; a responsive menu wraps them in the overlay markup
the reference emits.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\PostBlocks
classes.doc: The post-* blocks: they render the context's current post.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\QueryBlocks
classes.doc: query, post-template, query-title, query-no-results, query-pagination, term-description.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\Structure
classes.doc: template-part, pattern, site-title, site-tagline, site-logo.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Elements
classes.doc:
Per-block element styles (style.elements in a block's attributes, the
link colour most often). The reference gives each such block a
numbered wp-elements-N class and a rule per element state, emitted with
the page's support styles in render order.

methods.name: className
methods.doc: The block's wp-elements-N class, recording its rules; null when the block styles no element.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\ImageTags
classes.doc: The attributes the reference adds to an that carries a wp-image-{id} class: loading, decoding, width and height (prepended, in that order), and srcset plus sizes (appended). The srcset lists the displayed size first, then every same-ratio size in stored order, then the original.

methods.name: enrich
methods.signature: enrich(string $html, bool $withDataId = false, bool $front = false, bool $autoSizes = true): string
methods.doc: Rewrites every wp-image-* in a fragment; other images pass through.

methods.name: featured
methods.doc:
A post's featured image at full size, in the reference's attribute
order (dimensions, source, class, alt, style, then the loading
attributes and the srcset). Empty when the attachment has no file.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Layout
classes.doc:
The layout-support classes the reference adds at render time. Every
container carries is-layout-{type} and {block}-is-layout-{type}; flex and
grid layouts with rules of their own also carry a wp-container-* class
whose suffix names their generated stylesheet.

That suffix is a digest the engine cannot reproduce (its inputs are not
observable), so the engine derives its own deterministic suffix from the
layout attributes. Same shape, different value: recorded in the contract,
and the parity suites normalise it.

methods.name: classes
methods.signature: classes(string $blockSlug, array $attrs, string $defaultType = 'flow', bool $alwaysContainer = false): array

methods.name: declarations
methods.doc: The declarations behind a container class, in the reference's order.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Parser
classes.doc:
Parses block markup into a tree. The grammar is the delimiter comment:
an opener with optional JSON attributes, a closer, or a self-closing
void block; a name without a namespace is core/. Anything outside a
block is a freeform block that renders as-is.

methods.name: contains
methods.doc: Whether serialized content carries a block by name; a bare name means core/, and core blocks are also found by their short delimiter.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\QueryVars
classes.doc: The query variables a Query Loop block's context asks for, the way the reference's query block builds them.

methods.name: fromContext
methods.signature: fromContext(?array $context, int $page, array $sticky, callable $postTypeExists, callable $taxonomyViewable): array
shapes: @param list<int> $sticky the site's sticky post ids

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\RenderState
classes.doc:
Per-request rendering state. The reference numbers galleries, style
variations, and search inputs from ONE counter that runs across every
block rendered in the request (a list response keeps counting from post
to post), so the counter lives here, not on any block.

methods.name: nextImage
methods.doc: Content images seen so far in this page, for the loading rules.

methods.name: refundImages
methods.doc:
Images a plugin's block filter removed from the page give their budget
back, so the next image still counts as if the hidden ones never rendered.

methods.name: claimPriority
methods.doc: True once, for the image that gets fetchpriority="high".

methods.name: recordContainer
methods.doc: A container stylesheet this page needs: the class and its declarations.

methods.name: recordBlock
methods.doc: Every block name the page rendered; the stylesheet prints block styles for these only.

methods.name: nextElements
methods.doc: The next wp-elements-N class; the reference numbers these apart from the shared counter.

methods.name: uniqueLabel
methods.doc: A navigation's aria-label: the label itself the first time, then "label N" for repeats.

methods.name: enterNavigation
methods.doc:
A page list renders plain on its own and takes the navigation block's
item classes, submenu toggles, and interactivity only while it sits
inside one, so the navigation block marks the span it owns.

methods.name: enter
methods.doc: Marks a nested source as being rendered; false when it is already open (a cycle).

methods.name: descend
methods.doc: True while the block tree is shallower than the cap; deeper blocks render as nothing.

methods.name: depth
methods.doc: How deep the block tree is right now; zero outside a page render.

methods.name: setPendingElements
methods.doc: A dynamic block claims its element class before rendering, so a block that renders nothing still counts.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Renderer
classes.doc:
Renders a block tree the way the reference renders post_content:
delimiters gone, each block's own HTML kept with inner blocks rendered
in place, then the per-block render-time additions (layout classes, the
paragraph class, image attributes, gallery ids, style-variation
counters), and finally texturize over the whole.

methods.name: numberedStyle
methods.doc: The numbered companion of a registered style variation, consuming a counter; null when none applies.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Selector
classes.doc: The CSS selector a block type declares for its root or for one feature, from its `selectors` map or the older per-support keys.

methods.name: resolve
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $selectors the block type's selectors map
@param array<string, mixed> $supports the block type's supports
@param string|list<string>|null $target 'root', a dotted feature path, or a path list

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Styles
classes.doc:
The inline style and class names a block's "style" and preset
attributes produce at render time, for the dynamic blocks that build
their own wrapper (static blocks already carry them in stored markup).

methods.name: value
methods.doc:
var:preset|spacing|40 becomes var(--wp--preset--spacing--40). A value
that could close a declaration or a style element, or carry code,
is dropped: these values come from stored block attributes.

methods.name: slug
methods.doc: A class-name token from an attribute: letters, digits, dashes, underscores; nothing that ends an attribute.

methods.name: inline
methods.doc:
The style attribute's declarations. The reference emits the style
groups in a fixed order (border, colour, typography, spacing,
dimensions) and most properties in a fixed order within a group,
but a spacing box's sides come out as the block stored them.

methods.name: classes
methods.doc: The preset classes (font size, text alignment, custom class names) a block's attributes declare.

methods.name: align
methods.doc: The align class an "align" attribute declares.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Supports
classes.doc:
The wrapper attributes a block's supports declaration earns from its
attributes: align and class-name classes, color and gradient presets or
inline values, the font-size preset, the anchor id.

methods.name: attributes
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $attributes the block's prepared attributes
@param array<string, mixed> $supports the block type's supports
@param callable(string): string $kebab the slug form of a preset name (filtered on the reference)
@return array<string, string> class, style, id, only those that apply

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Wrapper
classes.doc:
The opening tag of a dynamic block's wrapper, in the reference's class
order: text alignment, the link-colour marker (for the blocks that
carry it), the block's own extra classes (a taxonomy, an alignment),
the custom class and its numbered style companion, the element-style
class, the block's class, colour presets, font size and family, and
the layout classes last; the style attribute inline.

methods.name: open
methods.signature: open(string $tag, string $blockClass, Minn\Blocks\Block $block, bool $styleFirst = false, string $blockName = '', bool $linkColorClass = false, array $extraClasses = array ( ), array $trailingClasses = array ( )): string

classes.name: Minn\Cli\AssetUpdate
classes.doc:
Shared wording for `wp plugin update` and `wp theme update`. Captured
from the reference: missing plugins warn and count as failed; a missing
theme is a fatal Error and stops. json/csv print only the rows (empty
stdout when nothing changed). `--exclude` always prints the skipped
line in table/summary, even when the list is empty.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\CacheCommand
classes.doc: `wp cache flush`: the engine has no object cache, so this is a no-op success.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc:
Flushes the object cache.

The engine does not run an object cache. The verb still succeeds so
fleet scripts that call it after a write do not abort.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Commands
classes.doc:
The verbs the engine answers to. Every one is registered for the
before_wp_load phase, which WP-CLI runs before it looks for WordPress,
and each replaces the bundled subcommand of the same name (a deferred
addition lands after the bundle and overrides its leaf).

classes.name: Minn\Cli\DirectorySearch
classes.doc:
Shared wording for `wp theme search` and `wp plugin search`. The
default table is name/slug/rating; Success prints before the rows and
only for table/yaml. json/csv/count print the Formatter output alone.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Installer
classes.doc:
The swap, both ways. Install parks WordPress's own files beside the
webroot, lays the engine and its shape files down, and leaves
wp-config.php and wp-content untouched; eject puts every parked file
back and removes what install wrote. A manifest in minn/.install.json
is the record eject works from. Preflight says what the site will and
will not get before anything moves.

methods.name: themeKind
methods.doc:
Same line Theme::active / ClassicTheme::active draw: a block template
index (child or parent) is a block theme; otherwise a parent index.php
is a classic theme.

methods.name: preflight
methods.doc: What the site will and will not get; the worst light decides install.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\MaintenanceCommand
classes.doc:
`wp maintenance-mode`: the `.maintenance` marker in the webroot. The
engine does not take the public site down while the file is present;
fleet scripts still need the verb to succeed so an update can bookend
itself with activate/deactivate.

methods.name: activate
methods.doc: Activates maintenance mode.

methods.name: deactivate
methods.doc: Deactivates maintenance mode.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: Displays maintenance mode status.

methods.name: is_active
methods.doc: Detects maintenance mode status. Exit 0 when active, 1 when not.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\MinnCommand
classes.doc:
Identifies the engine.

## EXAMPLES

wp minn version
wp minn info
wp minn probe

methods.name: version
methods.doc: Prints the engine version.

methods.name: probe
methods.doc:
Prints the inventory CaptainCore gathers from inside WordPress:
plugins, themes, must-use plugins, core version, home. One
`key:value` line per field; JSON values have no newlines. Split
on the first colon only.

methods.name: info
methods.doc: Prints the engine's version and where it runs from.

methods.name: cron
methods.doc: Runs the engine's scheduled work: due posts go live, expired rows are swept.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc:
Sends a test email through the site's mail settings.

## OPTIONS

<to>
: The address to send to.

methods.name: preflight
methods.doc:
Says what a WordPress webroot will and will not get from the engine.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot to inspect. Defaults to the current directory.

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
Parks WordPress and installs the engine into a webroot.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot. Defaults to the current directory.

[--park=<dir>]
: Where WordPress's own files go. Defaults to wp-parked beside the webroot.

[--force]
: Install even when preflight is RED.

methods.name: eject
methods.doc:
Removes the engine and puts WordPress's files back.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot. Defaults to the current directory.

methods.name: status
methods.doc:
Says whether a webroot runs WordPress or the engine.

## OPTIONS

[<webroot>]
: The webroot. Defaults to the current directory.

methods.name: scripts
methods.doc:
The site's script pack: the GPL `wp-*` JavaScript packages the engine
does not reimplement, which a few plugin front ends need (the
WooCommerce block cart and checkout). The engine never ships them;
this installs them into the site's own wp-content, from the
WordPress the swap parked beside the webroot, or from any WordPress
tree named with --from.

## OPTIONS

[<action>]
: status (the default), install, or remove.

[--from=<path>]
: A WordPress tree to take the packages from. Defaults to the parked
copy the install recorded.

methods.name: recovery
methods.doc:
The extensions recovery paused after they killed a request, and the
way back. A plugin or theme that fatals is paused so the next
request answers without it; nothing loads it again until it is
resumed here.

## OPTIONS

[<action>]
: status (the default), resume, or resume-all.

[<name>]
: For resume: the plugin file or theme slug to let back in.

[--theme]
: Treat the name as a theme rather than a plugin.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\OptionCommand

Options, read and written straight to the options table. Serialized

"name": "Block Visibility for Minn",
"version": "1.0.0",
"license": "MIT",
"replaces": ["block-visibility/block-visibility.php"],
"autoload": {"Minn\\Ext\\BlockVisibility\\": "src/"},

"shortcodes": ["example_tag"],

classes.name: Minn\Front\Resolver
classes.doc:
Turns a public URL into a Resolution, following the reference's observed
rules:

- Unpaged content and archives without a trailing slash redirect to the
slashed form, as typed (case kept); paged views, search, and 404s do not.
- Query-var forms (?p=, ?page_id=, ?cat=, ?tag=, ?author=, ?m=, ?name=,
?pagename=) redirect to the pretty form when the target is public.
- Archive-shaped paths (category, tag, author, search, a four-digit year)
are strict: a mismatch is a 404 with no guessing.
- Plain-segment paths try the page hierarchy, then the post structure,
then redirect to the closest published page or post whose name starts
with the last segment, pages before posts, newest first.
- Empty term and date archives are 404; an author archive is 200 for any
name, even one that belongs to nobody.
- Non-public posts are 404 to anonymous readers and served to a reader
who can edit them.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Recovery

kills a request, the file it died in names it, the engine records it as
paused, and the next request loads without it: the site comes back on
its own instead of staying down until a human reads the log.

The paused list is stored where WordPress stores it, in the same shape
(`paused_plugins` keyed by plugin file, `paused_themes` by stylesheet,
each holding type, file, line and message), so a site that ejects back
to WordPress finds the pause it left with.

is never paused: a fatal in the engine or in core is not a plugin's
fault and pausing something would not fix it.

does not reimplement, which a few plugins' front ends need (WooCommerce's
block cart and checkout are the reason it exists).

These packages are GPL, so the engine never ships them: the SITE installs
them into its own `wp-content`, the way it installs a language pack, and
the engine registers the handles only when they are actually there. A
site owner adding GPL files to a site that already runs GPL plugins is
not the engine distributing GPL; nothing under `minn/` changes.

The engine's own MIT packages under `minn/assets/wp` always win: the pack
fills the gaps around them, it does not replace them.

constants.value: array (   'a' =>    array (     0 => 'href',     1 => 'title',     2 => 'rel',   ),   'abbr' =>    array (     0 => 'title',   ),   'acronym' =>    array (     0 => 'title',   ),   'b' =>    array (   ),   'blockquote' =>    array (     0 => 'cite',   ),   'cite' =>    array (   ),   'code' =>    array (   ),   'del' =>    array (     0 => 'datetime',   ),   'em' =>    array (   ),   'i' =>    array (   ),   'q' =>    array (     0 => 'cite',   ),   's' =>    array (   ),   'strike' =>    array (   ),   'strong' =>    array (   ), )

methods.name: text
methods.doc: Plain text: tags gone, whitespace collapsed, control characters dropped.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: A URL for a stored field: empty when its scheme is not one the reference allows.

methods.name: attributeUrl
methods.doc: A URL inside markup: an unsafe scheme is cut off and the rest kept, as the reference does.

methods.name: style
methods.doc: A style attribute's value with only the listed properties kept.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Lists
classes.doc:
List shaping behind the facade's array utilities: the multi-field sort
wp_list_sort() promises (loose comparison per field, first difference
wins) and the row-shape conversions wpdb hands back for its OBJECT_K /
ARRAY_A / ARRAY_N output formats.

methods.name: shapeRows
methods.doc:
Rows of stdClass shaped for a wpdb output format: keyed by their first
column (first row wins a duplicate key), associative, or numeric.

methods.name: descendants
methods.signature: descendants(array $items, int $rootId, callable $id, callable $parent, array $visited = array ( )): array
methods.doc:
Every descendant of one root in a flat parent-linked list, preorder
(a child ahead of its own children), the shape _get_term_children and
get_page_children walk. Visited ids guard against a parent cycle.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Locale
classes.doc:
The locale's calendar and number vocabulary as data: the names a site
prints for weekdays, months and meridiems, and how it separates
thousands and decimals.

The names are English here because the engine carries no core
translations yet; the facade runs each one through the translation
filters on the way out, so a catalogue can answer for them later
without this class changing.

methods.name: weekdayInitial
methods.doc: A weekday's one-letter form.

methods.name: abbreviation
methods.doc: A weekday's or month's three-letter form; May is already three letters.

methods.name: monthKey
methods.doc: Months are keyed by their zero-padded number, both ways round.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Markers
classes.doc:
The BEGIN/END marker blocks insert_with_markers() maintains in files like
.htaccess: the captured shape keeps everything outside the markers,
replaces the block inside them, and writes the reference's four-line
do-not-edit preamble ahead of the inserted lines.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Paths
classes.doc: File-system path and permission spellings.

methods.name: translationDir
methods.doc:
The trailing-slashed directory holding a text domain's {domain}-{locale}.mo:
a custom path first, then the language dir's plugins and themes folders,
then the dir itself for the default domain; false when none has the file.

methods.name: normalize
methods.doc: Forward slashes only, runs collapsed, a stream wrapper kept, a Windows drive letter upper-cased.

methods.name: symbolicMode
methods.doc: The `ls -l` spelling of a mode: type letter, then rwx for owner, group and world with the setuid, setgid and sticky bits folded in.

classes.name: Minn\Support\SearchReplace
classes.doc:
String replace that walks serialized-PHP arrays of scalars without
unserialize, so a domain change in an option blob keeps its lengths.

methods.name: in
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: int} replacement and how many times $old occurred

classes.name: Minn\Support\Serialized
classes.doc:
Tolerant readers for the serialized-PHP blobs WordPress stores. Nothing
here executes the blob; each reader scans for the one shape it needs.

constants.name: INVALID
constants.doc: Returned by decode() when the blob is not a serialized value the reader accepts.

methods.name: stringList
methods.doc: The string values of a serialized string list.

methods.name: serializeStringList
methods.doc: A flat string list in the stored form.

methods.name: field
methods.doc: The first "field";value pair inside a blob: string, int, or float value as a string.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc:
A serialized scalar or array as PHP data, parsed by this reader:
strings, integers, floats, booleans, null, and arrays of those.
Objects are refused (nothing here instantiates anything), as is any
blob with trailing bytes or a malformed shape, with INVALID.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc:
PHP's serialize() for the values decode() accepts: null, bool, int,
float, string, and arrays of those. Objects are refused.

methods.name: intList
methods.doc: The integer values of a serialized list such as sticky_posts.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Time
classes.doc: Human-scale spans: a number of seconds as the largest whole unit it fills, rounded, never below one.

methods.name: span
shapes: @return array{0: int, 1: string} count and unit name

classes.name: Minn\Support\Url
classes.doc:
URL shaping the escaping and query helpers share: the character cleanup
esc_url applies, bracket encoding outside the authority, and query
argument merging. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/functions.json.

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: Spaces encoded, stray characters dropped, ";//" healed, a bare host given http; '' when nothing survives.

methods.name: encodeBrackets
methods.doc: Square brackets after the authority are percent-encoded; the authority itself is left alone. @param array<string, mixed> $parsed

methods.name: withQuery
methods.doc:
The URI with query arguments merged in (false removes one), the
fragment kept, a bare query string treated as such.
shapes: @param Closure(array): array $encode encodes the existing arguments the way the reference does
@param Closure(array): string $build builds the query string

methods.name: validateForHttp
methods.doc:
The checks wp_http_validate_url makes on a URL whose protocol already
passed: an http(s) scheme, a host without credentials or a colon, no
private address unless it is this site or allowed, only the usual
ports (or the site's own). Returns the URL, or null when refused.
shapes: @param Closure(string, string): bool $externalAllowed whether a private host may be fetched anyway

methods.name: buildQuery
methods.doc: A query string in the reference's spelling: nested keys as `a%5Bb%5D`, null as a bare key, booleans as 0/1.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: parse_url that also accepts scheme-relative and path-only URLs; a single component by its PHP_URL_* constant.

methods.name: withScheme
methods.doc: The URL under a scheme, or scheme-and-host stripped for 'relative'; a protocol-relative URL is read as http first.

methods.name: safeRedirect
methods.doc:
A redirect target the site may send a browser to: http(s) only, no
credentials, and a host the caller allows (local paths always pass).
shapes: @param Closure(string): list<string> $allowedHosts the hosts allowed for the target's host

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ArchiveTitle
classes.doc:
The label and name an archive titles itself with: `Category:` around the
term, `Author:` around the display name, the date formatted for its
granularity. One source of truth for the block path's query-title and
the classic path's get_the_archive_title(), which used to compute the
same labels separately. Search and post-type archives stay with their
callers: their captured shapes differ between the two paths.

methods.name: parts
shapes: @return array{string, string} the label (no colon) and the escaped bare name; both empty when the view has none

methods.name: compose
methods.doc: The reference's prefixed shape: `Category: Uncategorized`.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\BodyClasses
classes.doc:
The body-class list a classic theme's body_class() starts from, in the
reference's order: the query tokens (with the singular and template
tokens spliced in front of the type token), logged-in, the embed and
theme tokens, with the numbered paging tokens re-seated after the embed
token. The body_class filter runs over this list in the facade.

methods.name: classic
methods.signature: classic(Minn\Front\Resolution $resolution, array $coreClasses, ?string $customTemplate, bool $privacyPage, bool $loggedIn, bool $customLogo, bool $embedResponsive, string $themeSlug, ?string $parentSlug, bool $bar): array

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicContent
classes.doc:
What a classic theme's the_content() prints: the engine's block pipeline
(render, password gate, the more-tag teaser in listings), the cached
embeds, then the runtime's shortcodes and the_content filters so plugin
code sees the same hook order the reference runs.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicRenderer
classes.doc:
A whole page from the active classic theme: the reference's PHP template
loader. The main query stands, template_redirect fires, the hierarchy
picks a PHP file, template_include filters it, and load_template() runs
it as the response body. The theme prints its own document; the engine
contributes the reference's wp_head defaults (title tag, robots, feed
links, REST and oEmbed discovery, canonical, site icon) as hooks the
theme's wp_head() call fires.

methods.name: create
methods.signature: create(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme $theme, ?Minn\Theme\Theme $styleTheme, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, int $perPage, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL): self

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme
classes.doc:
The active classic (PHP-template) theme on disk. A theme is classic when
it ships no block template index; its templates are PHP files the engine
dispatches through the reference's hierarchy and runs via load_template().
The theme's own functions.php loads through the runtime's symbol gate.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Folder
classes.doc: A theme folder read from disk: its style.css headers, which folder its templates come from, its screenshot, whether it is a block theme.

methods.name: read
shapes: @param array<string, string> $labels key => the style.css header label
@param Closure(string, array<string, string>): array<string, string>|null $reader the header reader (the facade's, so header filters apply); the engine's own by default

methods.name: screenshot
methods.doc: The screenshot file name, or null when the theme has none.

methods.name: isBlockTheme
shapes: @param list<string> $dirs the stylesheet and template directories

methods.name: filePath
methods.doc: The first of the stylesheet and template directories that holds the file, or the template directory's path.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\GlobalStyles
classes.doc:
theme.json to CSS. Presets become custom properties on :root and their
has-* utility classes; settings.layout sizes, root styles, elements, and
per-block styles become rules; the containers, galleries, and style
variations the page actually rendered get their own stylesheets. The
layout rules themselves (flow, constrained, flex, grid, alignments) are
the engine's own, written to the same class hooks.

methods.name: styles
methods.doc: The theme.json (plus site-editor) styles node, under the engine's own defaults.

methods.name: resolvedStyles
methods.doc:
The same node with every `var:preset|…` token resolved to the custom
property it names, which is the shape a caller reading the styles as
data expects (the CSS writer resolves them on the way out instead).

methods.name: presetList
methods.doc:
A preset list as theme.json writes it is a plain list; as the site
editor saves it, it is keyed by origin (default, theme, custom). The
reference prints the origins in that order, so the two shapes flatten
to one list here.

methods.name: fontFaces
methods.doc:
The @font-face rules for every family that declares font files, as
the reference prints them in its own style element: family (quoted
when it has a space), style, weight, display, then the sources with
file:./ resolved against the theme that carries the file and the
format named from the extension. Families without files print
nothing.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\HeadLinks
classes.doc:
The links the reference puts in every head: the site and comments
feeds (plus the archive's own feed), the REST discovery link, the
JSON alternate for the queried object, and the site icon set. The
block path prints them as one run; the classic path prints the same
pieces from the reference's wp_head hooks.

methods.name: restLink
methods.doc: No trailing newline: the reference prints the JSON alternate and the RSD link on the same physical line.

methods.name: shortlink
methods.doc: Singular views only; posts and pages alike shortlink as ?p={id}, in the reference's single quotes.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Hierarchy
classes.doc:
The classic template hierarchy: the candidate file names each template
type tries, most specific first, as the reference resolves them. The
facade's get_{type}_template() functions feed these to get_query_template(),
which locates the first candidate the theme (child, then parent) ships.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\MainQueryBridge
classes.doc:
Stands the main query for a themed page: a plugin's archive runs through
WP_Query (pre_get_posts shapes it), everything else is the engine's own
listing seeded into the query globals. Then the front-end lifecycle
fires: "wp" with the request object, then template_redirect.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\PageRenderer
classes.doc:
A whole page from the active block theme: the template the resolution
maps to, rendered against the main query, inside the document shell the
reference emits (skip link, wp-site-blocks, the skip-link target on the
first main element).

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Content\Posts $posts, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, Minn\Theme\Templates $templates, Minn\Blocks\Renderer $renderer, int $perPage, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL, ?Minn\Theme\MainQueryBridge $bridge = NULL, ?Minn\Theme\HeadLinks $headLinks = NULL)

methods.name: create
methods.signature: create(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, int $perPage, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL): self

methods.name: bodyClasses
methods.doc:
The reference's body-class tokens: the singular and template tokens
sit in front of the type token ("page", "single"), the custom-logo
and embed tokens follow the core set, the paging tokens come after
those, and the theme (and child theme) tokens close the list.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\PatternText
classes.doc:
Block-theme patterns are PHP files whose only code is a handful of
echo-and-escape calls around literal strings. The engine never executes
them: it interprets that small text grammar (string literals, "."
concatenation, the i18n and escaping wrappers, the theme URI helper, and
printf with %s) and leaves anything else out. The header comment block
is dropped, and every byte outside the PHP tags is kept as-is.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateIndex
classes.doc:
Every block template and template part the site offers, in the order the
reference lists them: the rows the site editor saved first (newest post
date first), then the theme's own files in the order the directory hands
them back, then whatever a plugin registered. A saved row shadows the
theme file of the same slug and reports has_theme_file so the file can
be restored by deleting the row.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: Null when the id names another theme, or a slug nothing provides.

methods.name: authorText
methods.doc:
Who the caller is told made this: the theme's own name for anything
that has a file behind it, the plugin for a registered one, the
author's display name for a row a person saved, and the site's name
when nobody is recorded.

methods.name: originalSource
methods.doc: theme when a file backs it, plugin when one registered it, user when someone saved it, else site.

methods.name: isCustom
methods.doc: A slug the reference does not name in its default template types is a custom template.

methods.name: markup
methods.doc:
Markup as a caller of the REST route sees it: patterns spliced in
where the template only named them, then every template-part block
told which theme it belongs to. A record carries the markup as
stored, because that is what get_block_templates() hands a plugin.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplatePartTheme
classes.doc:
A template-part block inside a template says which theme's part it means.
The theme's own files usually leave that out, and the reference fills the
active theme in on the way out, for saved rows as much as for files. It
appends the attribute and leaves every other byte of the markup alone.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplatePatterns
classes.doc:
A template can name a pattern instead of carrying its blocks, and the
reference hands the caller the blocks: every "wp:pattern" delimiter is
replaced by the pattern's own markup before a template or part is
served. A slug the theme does not know stays exactly as it is, which is
what tells an editor the pattern went missing rather than the block.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateRecord
classes.doc:
One block template or template part, whatever it came from: a theme
file, a row the site editor saved, or a template a plugin registered.
The id every caller uses is "<theme>//<slug>" in all three cases.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $theme, string $slug, string $type, string $content, string $title, string $description, string $source, ?string $origin, bool $hasThemeFile, int $author, ?string $modified, ?string $date, int $wpId, string $status = 'publish', ?string $area = NULL, ?string $plugin = NULL)

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateWriter
classes.doc:
Saving and removing block templates. A template the theme ships is never
touched on disk: editing one writes a wp_template row that shadows the
file, and deleting that row is what "reset to the theme version" means.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
Writes the site's own copy of a template, creating the row the first
time. Returns the post id.
shapes: @param array{title?: string, content?: string, description?: string, area?: string} $fields

methods.name: trash
methods.doc: Moves a site copy to the trash, which hands the theme's file back.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Templates
classes.doc:
Which template renders a resolution, and where its markup comes from:
a wp_template post saved from the site editor (matched by slug and the
theme term) wins over the theme's file. Parts resolve the same way
through wp_template_part.

methods.name: candidates
methods.doc: The block-theme template hierarchy for each kind of resolution.

methods.name: userStyles
methods.doc: The site editor's saved global styles for the active theme, when any.

methods.name: customTemplate
methods.doc: A page's chosen custom template, from _wp_page_template meta.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Theme
classes.doc:
The active block theme on disk, read as data: theme.json, the templates
and parts directories, and the patterns index. A child theme's files
win and its parent fills in what the child does not define; theme.json
merges the same way, with the child's preset lists replacing the
parent's whole. The engine reads the site's installed theme the way it
reads the site's database; it never runs the theme's PHP.

methods.name: forStyles
methods.doc:
The active theme as styling data (theme.json present), whether or not
it is a block theme; the classic renderer prints its presets where the
reference prints a classic theme's global styles.

methods.name: parentSlug
methods.doc: The theme's own name, and the parent's, for body classes.

methods.name: merge
methods.doc:
Layered theme.json: maps merge key by key, lists (palettes, font
sizes, template parts) replace as a whole.

methods.name: name
methods.doc:
The theme's display name, as the stylesheet header states it; a child
theme answers with its own. Falls back to theme.json's title, then the
folder name.

methods.name: fileSlugs
methods.doc:
Every template (or part) slug the theme offers, the child's files
first and the parent's after, each in the order the directory hands
them back: the reference walks these directories unsorted and its
template list carries that order through.

methods.name: customTemplate
methods.doc: A template title and description the theme declares for a custom template slug.

methods.name: partTitle
methods.doc: The title theme.json gives a template part, when it names one.

methods.name: partArea
methods.doc: The template-part area declared in theme.json (header, footer, or uncategorized).

methods.name: pattern
methods.doc: A pattern's markup, with its PHP text subset interpreted; null when unknown.

methods.name: patternMeta
methods.doc:
A pattern's declared Block Types and Categories, the header fields a
plugin reads to tell (say) a header pattern from any other.

methods.name: patternHeader
methods.doc:
The header fields a pattern declares, as the metadata attribute the
reference writes onto the pattern's first block when it splices the
pattern into a template. A field the header omits is omitted here.
shapes: @return array{patternName: string, name: string, description?: string, categories?: list<string>}|null

methods.name: styleUri
methods.doc: The theme's stylesheet URL when it ships one; a child's own, else nothing (the parent's is not enqueued for it).
